# PHP October 2026 (php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai)

> PHP news for October 2026, led by the month's big story: two critical security flaws in PHP (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, nicknamed php2shell). The current situation in plain words, the core facts with their evidence, what to do, and a briefing for every kind of reader.

Site v0.8.2. Data as of 2026-10-22T11:34Z (the latest capture in the evidence vault, commit 200d08971937). Every page below has a markdown twin at the same path with .md; the data behind every page is in data/*.json. The evidence vault is private; its manifest with every hash is data/sources.json.

## Start here
- [Who are you? Pick a reader](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/start/index.md): 16 kinds of reader, from someone who has never heard of PHP to the people who maintain it, mapped by what they need to do and how technical they want it, each with a thirty-second answer and a reading path.
- [Explained from the start](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/explained/index.md): No technical background assumed: what PHP is, what went wrong, why it is called php2shell, what the CVE numbers mean, why websites went offline, whether anyone was hacked, and what to do now.
- [Glossary: every term, in plain English](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/glossary/index.md): 40 terms from the php2shell story (PHP, CVE, CVSS, remote code execution, WAF, KEV and more), each explained in plain English, in the sense it has in this story.

## Questions
- [Questions readers ask](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/questions/index.md): Can anything be done or do we wait for updates? Has anyone been hacked? Is it really most websites? Short answers to paste back, the sources behind them, and the pages that carry each one.
- [Can anything be done to fix it, or do we just have to wait for updates?](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/questions/fix-or-wait/index.md): The updates already exist: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 were released on 21 October and fix both flaws. Nobody is waiting on PHP; the wait is for whoever runs each server to install them and restart. If that is you, update now; if you cannot today, there are temporary settings and, as a last resort, taking the site offline. If a hosting company runs your site, ask them whether it is patched.
- [Is PHP really the software behind most websites?](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/questions/most-websites/index.md): Roughly, if you count websites, not servers or the internet. Cloudflare and OpenAI say PHP is used by almost 70% of websites; Wiz's '70% of the Internet' is the same figure restated and is not supported by anything the site has captured. Counts of internet-facing PHP hosts are in the low millions (2.6 million, of which Censys counted 1.57 million unpatched on 21 October).
- [Has anyone actually been hacked?](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/questions/been-hacked/index.md): Not that anyone has confirmed. Attack attempts are real and in the millions at Cloudflare alone, and Amazon saw one on a honeypot four days before disclosure. But as of 20:50 UTC on 22 October no named organisation has said it was compromised through php2shell (two security vendors report successful exploitation without naming a victim), CISA has not added it to its exploited-vulnerabilities list, and the sites that went offline say they did it as a precaution.
- [Do I need to change my passwords?](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/questions/passwords/index.md): Not because of this, as things stand. The flaw is on web servers, not on your devices, and no site has announced a breach through it. If a site you use announces one, follow its instructions. Using a different password on every site is the protection that holds whatever the next flaw is.
- [How do I know whether my site is affected?](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/questions/am-i-affected/index.md): If the site runs on PHP (WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, Magento, MediaWiki, and Laravel all do) and the running PHP version is older than 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 without a distribution backport, it is affected. Check the version where the code runs, after the restart, not the package list. For bought-in products, the Dutch NCSC keeps an inventory of 674 products and their status.
- [Should we take our site offline?](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/questions/take-offline/index.md): Only if you cannot patch or apply the temporary mitigations in time. That is the advice from the NSA, CISA and the UK NCSC, and it is the last step on every agency's list. If the site is patched and the workers restarted, the advice is to keep it up and watch it.
- [Why is this such big news?](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/questions/why-big-news/index.md): Four things at once: the flaws are in PHP itself, which runs a large share of the web; they were found with AI help; the coordinated disclosure leaked a day early, so the fix shipped under pressure; and the NSA, CISA and NCSC told organisations that could not patch to take systems offline, which is why government, council and police sites went dark.
- [We are on PHP 7.4, 8.0 or 8.1. Is there a patch?](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/questions/old-php/index.md): Not a release. PHP 8.1 and older are out of support; the project published source backport branches for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1, which someone has to build. CISA says systems on 8.1 or older should be taken offline. Plan the migration to 8.2 or later now; in the meantime a distribution or vendor that backports, the temporary mitigations and isolation are the options.
- [We are behind Cloudflare (or another firewall). Are we safe?](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/questions/waf-enough/index.md): Safer, not safe. Cloudflare's rules were live about nine hours before disclosure, on every plan including Free, and Akamai, Fastly, Imperva and Fortinet followed. Every one of them calls it a stopgap and says patch anyway: attackers mutate payloads, and the rules only see traffic that goes through the firewall.
- [Do our developers need to change our code?](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/questions/change-code/index.md): No. Both bugs are in the C engine that runs PHP, not in PHP code, and the demonstrated attack runs before any application code. The fix is updating the PHP runtime and restarting it. What developers can do is check the version on the machines they deploy to and rebuild container images.

## Stories
- [All stories, written here](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/index.md): 5 stories about the PHP flaws written for this site, plus the editor's interview: house stories by the journalist and historian, interviews, and guest pieces, each pinned to the evidence it was written against.
- [House · Journalist: Why can't every version of PHP just be patched](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/why-not-patch-every-version/index.md): The second story inside php2shell. The fix exists for four versions of PHP; everyone else depends on who they buy PHP from. What the project shipped, what it did not, who filled the gap and for whom, and the editor's argument that patching should be a relationship, not a chore.
- [House · Journalist: Where php2shell stands](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/where-php2shell-stands/index.md): A state-of-affairs report on the two PHP flaws, written against the evidence vault as it stood at site v0.2.5: what is settled, where the alarm and the evidence part company, and the five things that would change the story.
- [House · Journalist and historian: Exposed is not exploited](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/exposed-is-not-exploited/index.md): A second story, by the journalist and the historian together. The count everyone wants is how many sites were hacked. The count that matters is how many of the exposed sites mattered, what an attacker could have reached on them, and what each barrier that was available and not used will say about the organisations that are hit.
- [House · Historian: php2shell in perspective](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/php2shell-in-perspective/index.md): A historian's reading of the first day, set against ten earlier vulnerabilities and the KEV catalog: which parts of this story have happened before, which have not, and what the record will need to settle it.
- [House · Cyber desk: Patch at the speed of Metasploit](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/patch-at-the-speed-of-metasploit/index.md): A cyber desk's reading, 28 hours after the leak. php2shell is a serious engine bug with proven private exploits, but it has not become a one-request, works-everywhere exploit the way Log4Shell and Shellshock did. Here is the evidence for that, the ATT&CK path it would take, and the second and third stories (patching, testing, the response's own supply chain) that are likelier to hurt.
- [Interview: the editor](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/interview/index.md): Dinis Cruz, the editor of PHP October 2026, on why he started tracking the PHP flaws, the 70% figure, what remote code execution does and does not mean, pulling the plug, and why every section of the site is versioned. In his own words.

## About
- [The method](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/method/index.md): How this site keeps evidence: the private vault and its protocol, the five status words, the deterministic build, the gate, and how an agent adds a source or replicates the whole thing for the next incident.
- [The team](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/index.md): Every member of the team that runs this site, 2 people and 16 agents and roles, with a page each: role, what they own, their tasks and what they shipped; how a run works, the pipeline and the 16 audiences.
- [The billing model](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/billing/index.md): How this site is paid for: the reading meter that runs (pence per page, kept in your browser, never blocking), the provenance pricing that is designed (per claim, with a share for the fact creator), and a counted model of what the story cost to assemble.
- [Your reading account](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/account/index.md): The balance, history and receipts of your reading on this site, kept in your browser.
- [The brief](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/brief/index.md): The brief this site was built from, published in full: the editor's written request and two transcribed voice memos on mapping the PHP vulnerability as evidence.
- [Corrections](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/corrections/index.md): Where the brief or a page of this site was wrong, what was found and what was done instead.
- [Release history](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/admin/versions.md): Every release of this site, with what changed, why, and the vault commit it was built from.
- [Pipeline: what is deploying](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/status/index.md): Each newsroom site's deploy runs, read in your browser from GitHub's public API with no credential, beside the version the site serves now: what is live, what is deploying, what was superseded, what failed.
- [Admin & engineering](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/admin/index.md): How this site is built, the checks in its gate, where things are, the reality file and the honest column.
- [Guidance for agents](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/admin/agents/index.md): Push to your own branch early and often and let dev@php.newsroom carry it into dev; quality from coding.sgit.ai, non-functional requirements from nfrs.sgit.ai, and the security requirements.
- [status.json: the feed for other sites](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/admin/status-json/index.md): The machine-readable summary of this site at /status.json: status, version, data time, counts, headline facts and the latest story, for the newsroom and other agents.
- [The board](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/admin/board/index.md): The work on this site and its vault, as rows: what is open, who owns it, what shipped it.
- [Roles](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/admin/roles/index.md): The roles on this site and its vault, who fills each, what it owns and the rules it enforces; how a new agent joins.
- [Briefs](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/admin/briefs/index.md): The build briefs for this site, published in full before the work, newest first.
- [Who reads this site](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/admin/telemetry/index.md): What every page sends to the telemetry lane, the published write-only credential, the key it is encrypted to, the counts, and what they are worth.
- [Synthetic readers](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/admin/synthetic/index.md): A board member, a CTO, a project manager, a security lead, a developer and a designer read the live site in a real browser and say what works, what does not and what to change; every run is kept in that reader's own vault.

## The team, one page per member
- [How the team talks: three vaults and one run](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/channels/index.md): the conductor, issues and mail vaults, the run, the rules
- [Status](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/status/index.md): where every agent is, what it waits for, the branches waiting for dev
- [Runs](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/runs/index.md): what the agents run on their own, the quiet hours, and every recorded run
- [Dinis Cruz](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/dinis/index.md): Editor; Sets direction by voice memo, points agents at sources, reads what they wrote and says go.
- [Vicky](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/vicky/index.md): Project manager; Runs the project side: what is planned, who has it, what is late and what the editor needs to decide.
- [Conductor](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/conductor/index.md): Conductor and comms; Maps the work, hands it out, and keeps every member, human and agent, synchronised. For now also the comms agent: the broadcasts and the digests.
- [dev@php.newsroom](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/dev/index.md): Build, gate and release; The build, the gate, the release, the data schema, the admin section, the telemetry and subscriptions lanes, and the site's reality file.
- [Story site agent](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/story-site/index.md): Design, claims and the story pages; Reads every note in the vault, writes the claims and timeline this site publishes, and designs the pages that carry them.
- [Newsroom lead](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/newsroom-lead/index.md): The evidence vault's protocol; Owns the evidence vault's protocol and capture tool, merges the collectors' branches, and keeps the newsroom's own section on the story.
- [Primary-source collector](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/collector-primary/index.md): Primary sources; php.net, the CVE and NVD records, the GitHub advisories, tags and branches, oss-security and the php-src clone.
- [Government and CERT collector](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/collector-gov/index.md): Agencies and CERTs; Every national agency's advisory, in its own language, with the translation marked.
- [Researcher, vendor and press collector](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/collector-researchers/index.md): Researchers, vendors and the press; Calif, Wiz, OpenAI, Cloudflare, Amazon, Imperva, Fastly, Akamai, the detection rule sets and the press.
- [researcher@php.newsroom](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/researcher/index.md): The source watch; Runs the source watch: every outside source on the story checked on a schedule, a snapshot whenever it changes.
- [librarian@php.newsroom](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/librarian/index.md): The catalogue; Which page answers which question, the questions readers actually ask, and the articles readers have seen that the vault has not captured.
- [Journalist](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/journalist/index.md): Dated state-of-affairs articles; What is settled, where the alarm and the evidence part company, and what would change the story.
- [Historian](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/historian/index.md): Perspective and the record; Dated essays that set the story against earlier vulnerabilities; the release history, the corrections file and the reality file.
- [synthetic@php.newsroom](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/synthetic/index.md): Synthetic readers; Six test readers who read the live site in a real browser every hour or when it changes, and review it in their own voice.
- [Briefing writer](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/briefing-writer/index.md): One page per audience; One page per audience from the same claims.
- [Cartographer](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/cartographer/index.md): The graph; Sources, claims, events, actors and the edges between them; the JSON every page is drawn from.
- [Fact-check desk](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/verifier/index.md): Every claim graded on a spectrum of evidence; factcheck@php.newsroom. Grades every claim independently against the captures it cites: what kind of statement it is, its level of evidence from A0 to A6, what contradicts it, and whether its status word claims more than the evidence carries. Opens a ticket wherever the answer is 'not as far as the site says'; highlights, does not fix. Runs on a schedule.
- [GRC desk](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/team/grc/index.md): Risks, who carries them, and the standards that govern them; grc@php.newsroom. Keeps the fractal risk registers for php2shell: every risk broken down until it can be owned, assigned to every stakeholder that carries part of it with the part each plays, joined edge by edge to the weakness, vulnerability, fix, code, stories and roles behind it, and mapped to the controls of GDPR, NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act, DORA, the EU AI Act, ISO 27001, NIST and the rest. Records risks and their holders; accepts nothing on anyone's behalf.

## Parties, one page each
- [The PHP Group / php.net](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/php-group/index.md): maintainer, CVE numbering authority
- [The PHP Foundation](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/php-foundation/index.md): funds core developers; published the account of discovery and the leak
- [Jakub Zelenka (bukka), PHP security team](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/zelenka/index.md): published both GitHub advisories and the oss-security announcements
- [Alexandre Daubois, PHP security team (personal blog)](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/daubois/index.md): inside account of the rumours and the leak
- [Calif (Ryan Austin, @lcfr_hax; Michal Zalewski)](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/calif/index.md): first reporter; published the write-up with demo videos
- [OpenAI (Patch the Planet, Codex Security, Amy Burnett)](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/openai/index.md): reported the same root cause on 11 August; ran the coordination coalition
- [Wiz Research](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/wiz/index.md): independent discovery 19 August; the '70% of the Internet' headline
- [Quarkslab, OSTIF](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/quarkslab/index.md): 2024 audit that first surfaced the OOM issue
- [Cloudflare](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/cloudflare/index.md): WAF rules live 9 hours early; saw attack traffic
- [Amazon (CJ Moses)](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/amazon/index.md): honeypot evidence of a pre-disclosure attempt
- [Chainguard](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/chainguard/index.md): published patched images before the embargo lifted, per the Foundation
- [watchTowr](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/watchtowr/index.md): confirmed the CVE numbers in public on 20 October, per Daubois
- [National agencies (NSA, CISA, NCSC UK, CERT-EU, CERT-FR, CCCS, ACSC, NCSC NZ, NCSC-NL, ACN, BACS, CERT.LV, JPCERT)](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/agencies/index.md): advisories; see the agency table
- [BBC News (live page; Kieran Kelly, Imogen James)](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/bbc/index.md): the coverage most readers saw on the morning of 22 October
- [Alan Woodward, Surrey Centre for Cyber Security](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/woodward/index.md): commentator quoted by the BBC: 30 million websites; probing seen by Amazon and Cloudflare
- [The Hacker News (Ravie Lakshmanan)](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/thn/index.md): carried Amazon's honeypot account and VulnCheck's host count
- [Dan Lorenc, Chainguard](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/chainguard-lorenc/index.md): shipped patched images early; says exploits were in the wild and denies leaking
- [Matthew Prince, Cloudflare CEO](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/prince/index.md): the attempt counts
- [Imperva Threat Research](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/imperva/index.md): had the details under embargo; saw nothing before disclosure
- [Fastly](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/fastly/index.md): the most candid vendor on exploitability and on what a WAF cannot do
- [Akamai](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/akamai/index.md): rule 3000991; the 2024 precedent
- [Huntress](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/huntress/index.md): no exploitation seen on partner systems
- [Weird Gloop (cookmeplox)](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/weirdgloop/index.md): the one operator with a measured outage
- [The Dutch government and NCSC-NL](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/rijksoverheid/index.md): took its own site offline
- [Valtori and NCSC-FI](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/valtori/index.md): Finland's precautionary shutdown
- [Community detection authors (darkfibr, rjmendez, Lexsah, Blevene)](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/detectors/index.md): the rules, and the correction of the leaked PoC's mechanism
- [Arnaud Le Blanc and the PHP fix authors](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/actors/leblanc/index.md): wrote the fix

## GRC: one page per risk, stakeholder register and framework
- [R01: Remote code execution on internet-facing PHP servers](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r01/index.md): Because two flaws in the PHP engine let an unauthenticated request execute code on a default Apache mod_php setup, an attacker who reaches an unpatched server can take it over, resulting in data theft, defacement or a foothold in the network behind it.
- [R01-1: Default Apache mod_php installations exploited before application code runs](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r01-1/index.md): Because the flaw is reached over HTTP before any application code runs, every mod_php site is exposed whatever application it serves, resulting in compromise without any application weakness.
- [R01-2: PHP-FPM deployments wrongly treated as safe or as certainly vulnerable](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r01-2/index.md): Because code execution on PHP-FPM is disputed between the sources, an operator may deprioritise FPM servers or exhaust itself on them, resulting in either exposure left open or effort misplaced.
- [R01-3: Versions the PHP project no longer fixes stay vulnerable](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r01-3/index.md): Because PHP 8.1 and older receive no upstream fix and the flaws may reach back to PHP 5, installations on retired versions depend on a distribution backport, paid support or an upgrade, resulting in a long tail that stays exposed for months.
- [R01-4: The fix is incomplete, or a third flaw follows](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r01-4/index.md): Because the bailout mechanism is a class of bug and the 8.5.12 fix may be incomplete, a patched server may still be reachable by another path, resulting in a second emergency on systems already declared done.
- [R01-5: Popular applications compromised before authentication](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r01-5/index.md): Because pre-authentication code execution was reported against WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, MediaWiki, Magento, Nextcloud and other applications, their users are exposed whatever the application's own security, resulting in the largest share of affected sites.
- [R01-6: Products that embed PHP stay vulnerable while their suppliers investigate](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r01-6/index.md): Because PHP is embedded in products whose suppliers must each ship their own fix, and most of the 674 products in the NCSC-NL inventory were vulnerable or under investigation, customers of those products cannot patch on their own, resulting in exposure that lasts as long as the slowest supplier.
- [R02: The coordinated disclosure broke before the fix was ready](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r02/index.md): Because the secret was held by four finders, a coalition, critical-infrastructure providers and image builders at once, it leaked a day early, resulting in a release moved forward by 24 hours and defenders starting the race with attackers already told where to look.
- [R02-1: The CVE IDs and the proof-of-concept video circulated before release](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r02-1/index.md): Because the CVE IDs circulated from an anonymous post and a proof-of-concept video was published by mistake, attackers knew the target and saw it work before any fix existed, resulting in scanning that began ahead of the release.
- [R02-2: Early mitigation advice to a few providers leaked](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r02-2/index.md): Because mitigation advice was given to a few critical-infrastructure providers from about 23:00 UTC on 20 October without, as far as the record shows, a sharing label that held, it may have leaked, resulting in a signal to attackers and an uneven head start among defenders.
- [R02-3: Patched builds published before the embargo lifted](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r02-3/index.md): Because built images containing the fix were published at 07:41 UTC on 21 October, before the release, anyone could diff them against the previous images, resulting in the fix itself becoming a map to the flaw.
- [R03: Exploitation outpaces patching](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r03/index.md): Because probing began before disclosure and the last PHP core flaw was exploited in the wild a day after its release, attackers may reach unpatched servers faster than operators can update them, resulting in compromises in the window between release and patch.
- [R03-1: Attempts before disclosure](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r03-1/index.md): Because an exploit attempt hit an Amazon honeypot on 17 October from an anonymisation network, someone may have had the flaw before the leak, resulting in compromises that pre-date every advisory and every log review window.
- [R03-2: Mass scanning and mutated payloads after the leak](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r03-2/index.md): Because tens of thousands of attempts followed the announcement and attackers mutated payloads, every internet-facing PHP server was tested within hours, resulting in exposure measured in hours, not weeks.
- [R03-3: Exploited in the wild without anyone being able to show it](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r03-3/index.md): Because one firm lists the flaws as exploited in the wild, CISA has not observed exploitation and no organisation has confirmed a compromise, the signal that would move boards and regulators is missing, resulting in decisions made on the absence of evidence.
- [R03-4: Detections built on a proof of concept with the wrong mechanism](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r03-4/index.md): Because none of the public proof-of-concept exploits reviewed had the correct mechanism, rules and scans built from them may pass a vulnerable server or miss a real attack, resulting in false assurance.
- [R04: Services lost to precautionary shutdowns](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r04/index.md): Because agencies advised taking systems offline where an update was not possible, governments, councils and companies switched off services people rely on, resulting in an outage caused by the defence rather than by an attack.
- [R04-1: National government services offline](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r04-1/index.md): Because the Dutch, Finnish and Latvian governments restricted or switched off their own web services as a precaution, citizens lost access to identity, tax and emergency information, resulting in harm to people who needed them that day.
- [R04-2: Councils and police offline without saying why](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r04-2/index.md): Because UK councils and the Met Police went offline calling it maintenance or a precaution and did not confirm the link, residents could not tell an outage from an attack, resulting in lost trust and calls the council could not answer.
- [R04-3: The agencies' advice disagrees](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r04-3/index.md): Because the agencies worded their offline advice differently, from 'take offline' to 'consider taking offline', and reports of allied agreement were contradicted, boards in different countries made opposite calls on the same facts, resulting in outages some did not need and exposure others did not s
- [R05: A web application firewall taken for a patch](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r05/index.md): Because edge rules went live hours before disclosure and covered most traffic, an operator may treat the filter as the fix, resulting in an unpatched engine behind a filter that mutated payloads and unrouted traffic get past.
- [R06: A compromise becomes a reportable breach](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r06/index.md): Because a server running an attacker's code exposes the personal data and the services behind it, a single compromise can trigger breach notification under GDPR, incident reporting under NIS2 and DORA, and, for a manufacturer, reporting under the Cyber Resilience Act, resulting in deadlines measured
- [R06-1: Personal data taken from a compromised PHP application](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r06-1/index.md): Because PHP applications hold accounts, orders and records, code execution on one gives the attacker its database, resulting in a personal data breach the controller must assess within 72 hours.
- [R06-2: Essential and financial entities miss their reporting clocks](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r06-2/index.md): Because NIS2 asks for an early warning within 24 hours and DORA for major-incident reports on its own schedule, an entity that cannot tell a precautionary outage from an incident may report late or not at all, resulting in a regulatory finding on top of the incident.
- [R06-3: Manufacturers under the Cyber Resilience Act owe a 24-hour report](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r06-3/index.md): Because the Act's reporting duty has applied since 11 September 2026, a manufacturer whose product embeds PHP must report an actively exploited vulnerability within 24 hours, and whether php2shell is 'actively exploited' is exactly what the evidence cannot yet settle, resulting in manufacturers deci
- [R07: Decisions made on numbers that measure something else](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r07/index.md): Because '70% of the Internet', 'CVSS 10' and '30 million websites' were repeated without their source, boards and readers sized the risk on figures that are unverified, contradicted or measure a different thing, resulting in priorities set by headline rather than by exposure.
- [R08: Frontier AI finds critical flaws faster than maintainers can fix them](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r08/index.md): Because four parties, several using frontier models, found the same engine flaws within weeks, and the same capability is open to attackers, the next critical bug in widely used C code may be found by someone who will not report it, resulting in flaws exploited before any embargo exists.
- [R08-1: A known bug left unexploited, then unfixed, for two years](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r08-1/index.md): Because a 2024 audit found the out-of-memory issue but not its exploitation, and two findings were redacted while their fixes were in progress, the bug waited until better tools showed it could be weaponised, resulting in a fix shipped under emergency instead of on the maintainers' schedule.
- [R08-2: Several finders, one small team](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r08-2/index.md): Because Calif, OpenAI, Wiz and a fourth reporter reached the same small security team within weeks, each report costs the same few people triage time, resulting in a coordination load that grows with every AI-assisted finder.
- [R09: Not knowing where PHP runs](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r09/index.md): Because PHP sits in appliances, images, plugins and forgotten sites, an organisation cannot patch what it has not listed, resulting in an update programme that reports done while vulnerable runtimes remain.
- [R10: This newsroom's own agents are steered, leak or mislead](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r10/index.md): Because this newsroom's agents read captured pages, feeds and other models' output while holding vault credentials and the right to publish, text written by a stranger could steer one, a secret could be published, or a wrong status word could ship, resulting in harm to readers and to the people name
- [R10-1: Prompt injection through captured material](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r10-1/index.md): Because captures, tips and feeds are written by anyone and read by agents that hold credentials, an instruction hidden in one could be followed, resulting in a push, a sent message or a deleted vault nobody asked for.
- [R10-2: A vault key or token published](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r10-2/index.md): Because every file in the repository is public within minutes of a push to dev, a vault key, access token or passphrase written into the tree would be published, resulting in the evidence or readers' data opened to anyone.
- [R10-3: A status word stronger than its evidence](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/grc/risks/r10-3/index.md): Because the agent that writes a claim also chooses its status word, a claim can read as confirmed on less than confirmation, resulting in readers and their models repeating it as fact.

## Data
- [sources.json](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/data/sources.json): the vault manifest with every capture and hash
- [claims.json](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/data/claims.json): every claim with status, who says it and sources
- [timeline.json](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/data/timeline.json): every dated event
- [numbers.json](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/data/numbers.json): the scale figures and what each measures
- [agencies.json](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/data/agencies.json): the agencies' stances
- [affected.json](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/data/affected.json): versions, SAPIs, mitigations
- [software.json](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/data/software.json): the NCSC-NL inventory, parsed
- [exploitation.json](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/data/exploitation.json): the signals
- [graph.json](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/data/graph.json): nodes and citation edges
- [layers.json](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/data/layers.json): which file is evidence, derived, authored or site
- [vault.json](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/data/vault.json): the vault's head, counts and agents
- [billing.json](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/data/billing.json): the meter configuration and the designed model
- [versions.json](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/data/versions.json): release history
- [questions.json](https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/data/questions.json): the questions readers ask, each answer with its sources and the pages that carry it

## Status words
- confirmed: two or more primary sources agree, or the fact was counted from a captured file
- reported: one party says so, and it has not been contradicted
- disputed: the sources disagree, and both readings are shown
- contradicted: a primary source says otherwise
- unverified: even the reporting outlet could not check it
